messages:
Ben: quick design thread — proposing a throughput-weighted key throttling system that ties per-key/org rate limits to GPU pool utilization. TL;DR: adapt refill rates by backend saturation and give committed orgs proportional priority.
Maya: sounds promising. how is this different from the token-bucket drafts we discussed last month?
Ben: good q. differences are: 1) refill-rate = base_rate * (1 - pool_utilization) so buckets slow down as GPUs fill; 2) org_weighting: keys get shares based on commit tier + recent usage; 3) borrow/repay: allow short bursts above share by borrowing from a global soft-pool (repaid when utilization drops); 4) per-region pools and per-route overrides (latency-sensitive routes can have reserved credits).
Omar: concerns: latency-critical requests (chat) mustn't queue too long. how do we avoid head-of-line blocking if throttling is per-key?
Ben: plan: admission control layer that checks both token-bucket and an in-memory priority queue. Priority classes: realtime (chat), batch (embeddings), low (rerank). Realtime gets small reserved credits and faster refill but lower borrow allowance.
Priya: can we see a sample config? small snippet would help ops/console mapping.
Ben: sure — rough example: 
```
global: { borrow_capacity: 100_000, soft_shed_threshold: 0.92 }
pool_us-east-1: { base_refill_tps: 2000, reserve_realtime: 200, reserve_batch: 500 }
org_acme: { weight: 3, burst_capacity: 5000 }
key_x: { route_overrides: { /v1/chat: { reserve: 50 } } }
```
Maya: how do we calculate weight? is it purely financial (commit tier) or also historical consumption?
Ben: hybrid: weight = alpha * commit_tier + beta * recent_token_rate (smoothed 1h). default alpha=0.7, beta=0.3. that biases toward paid commitments but adapts to changing patterns.
Omar: metrics we should emit: per-pool_utilization, per-org_refill_rate, borrow_pool_size, 429_rate_by_route, avg_queue_ms_by_priority. plus traces for decisions.
Priya: rollout thoughts? I'd prefer staged rollout: 1) read-only simulator mode (no enforcement, just logs + drift metrics), 2) soft-enforce (warn + 429s with long Retry-After headers for a small % of keys), 3) full-enforce with canary orgs.
Ben: +1. also add an emergency reserve for SRE and infra (escape hatch) — used only when pool_utilization > 0.98.
Maya: any security/abuse edge-cases? bots that spin up lots of short-lived keys to game weight?
Ben: mitigate with key registration limits, sliding-window fraud detectors, and minimum-age requirement for auto-scaling weight increases. also tie weight changes to billing events.
Omar: implementation notes: prefer token counters in edge caches for low-latency check, sync to central store (etcd) every ~5s. borrow pool reconciliation runs every 1s. need careful clocking and monotonic counters.
Priya: will this interact with region failover? if us-east is saturated and us-west has spare, can we route traffic cross-region?
Ben: yes — smart-routing policy will surface asymmetric capacity and optionally reroute traffic for keys flagged as multi-region. default is no cross-region for private deployments unless customer opts-in.
backpressure-bot: note: recorded simulated run at 2026-05-12T14:05Z shows borrow_pool peaked at 78% and avg_queue_ms_realtime = 24ms.
Maya: next steps: Ben to draft a PR with design doc + simulation data. Omar to list infra constraints (etcd qps, cache memory). Priya to provide priority route list. I'll sync with biz on weight defaults.
Ben: assigned. aiming for prototype branch by end of next sprint. questions/objections?
Maya: none from me. :thumbsup:
Omar: small nit — make sure backoff headers use Retry-After in seconds and include machine-readable reason code.
Ben: noted. thanks everyone.
